symbols.name: ell
symbols.def: Local-polynomial order \(\ell=\lfloor\beta\rfloor\), with \(\ell=\beta-1\) when \(\beta\) is an integer.

symbols.name: p_min
symbols.def: Lower bound \(p_{\min}\) on every stratum probability.

symbols.name: delta_bar
symbols.def: Fixed upper envelope \(\bar\delta\) for the threshold sequence.

symbols.name: delta_n
symbols.def: Arbitrary deterministic threshold \(\delta_n\) at sample size \(n\).

symbols.name: pi_x
symbols.def: Borel function \(\pi_x\) whose defining conditional-density identity is imposed by \(\text{ass:conditional-density-law}\).

symbols.name: mu_x_P
symbols.def: The unique continuous function \(\mu_x^P\) that equals an almost-everywhere version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) and satisfies the declared Taylor-remainder Hölder condition.

symbols.name: Y_a
symbols.def: Potential-outcome process \(a\mapsto Y(a)\); joint measurability under the full-data law is imposed by \(\text{ass:consistency}\).

symbols.name: P_full
symbols.def: A full-data law \(P^{\mathrm F}\) for \(X,A,Y\) and the process \(a\mapsto Y(a)\), whose observed margin is \(P\).

symbols.name: psi_delta
symbols.def: Full-data clamp-policy mean \(\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y\{d_\delta(A)\}]\).

symbols.name: mathcal_M
symbols.def: Finite-stratum Hölder and polynomial-thinning model \(\mathcal M\).

symbols.name: h_n
symbols.def: Bandwidth \(h_n\) defined by the first crossing of the polynomial information balance.

symbols.name: M_kappa_rho
symbols.def: Normalized reference moment matrix \(M_{\kappa,\rho}=\{\int_0^1v_\ell(u)v_\ell(u)^\top(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du\}/\{\int_0^1(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du\}\) for \(\rho\in[0,\infty)\).

symbols.name: I_0
symbols.def: First deterministic sample block satisfying \(|I_0|\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), for the retained natural-course mean.

symbols.name: I_1
symbols.def: Second deterministic sample block satisfying \(|I_1|\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), for atom masses.

symbols.name: I_2
symbols.def: Third deterministic sample block satisfying \(|I_2|\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), for local regressions.

symbols.name: G_x
symbols.def: Unnormalized local Gram matrix \(G_x=\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,0\leq U_i\leq1\}v_\ell(U_i)v_\ell(U_i)^\top\), where \(U_i=(A_i-\delta_n)/h_n\).

symbols.name: w_ix
symbols.def: Intercept weight \(w_{ix}=\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,0\leq U_i\leq1\}e_0^\top G_x^{-1}v_\ell(U_i)\) on \(\Omega_x\), and \(w_{ix}=0\) off \(\Omega_x\).

symbols.name: CI_n
symbols.def: Bias-aware confidence interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) with a local atom fallback on singular-Gram events.

symbols.name: L_n_star
symbols.def: Minimax worst-case expected length \(L_n^\star=\inf_{C_n:\,\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in C_n\}\geq1-\alpha}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{len}(C_n)]\).

assumptions.condition: The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed from \(P\).
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and Borel set \(B\subseteq[0,1]\), \(P(A\in B\mid X=x)=\int_B\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\).

standard.name: Conditional absolute continuity for a continuous treatment

assumptions.condition: Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), \(a\mapsto Y(a)\) is a jointly measurable bounded potential-outcome process and \(Y=Y(A)\) almost surely.
Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and every \(a\in[0,1]\), \(\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(a)\mid X=x]=\mu_x^P(a)\).

novel.justification: This is an explicit author-imposed, pointwise, and non-testable compatibility restriction used only for optional causal interpretation. It is credible when the scientific model posits a well-defined intervention at every dose and a smooth structural conditional-mean response whose value agrees pointwise with the selected continuous observed-regression extension. It is not implied by consistency, conditional exchangeability, modified-policy support, observed-regression Hölder smoothness, or Díaz et al., and it is not a novelty contribution.

assumptions.condition: Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), for every \(a\in[0,1]\), \(Y(a)\) is conditionally independent of \(A\) given \(X\).

standard.name: Conditional exchangeability for a continuous treatment

assumptions.condition: For every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and Lebesgue-almost every \(a\in[0,1]\), \(c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa\).

novel.justification: The global two-sided measurable envelope is an explicit treatment-assignment design class. It contains beta-type assignment densities proportional to \(a^\kappa\) and their normalized bounded measurable tilts, representing protocols that suppress doses near a contraindicated boundary while permitting irregular assignment elsewhere. It is not asserted to follow from Gaiffas's regular-variation condition.

assumptions.condition: For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), an almost-everywhere version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) has a continuous extension \(\mu_x^P\) satisfying \(\left|\mu_x^P(t)-\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}(\mu_x^P)^{(j)}(s)(t-s)^j/j!\right|\leq L|t-s|^\beta\) for all \(s,t\in[0,1]\).

standard.name: Taylor-remainder formulation of Hölder outcome-regression smoothness

definitions.name: Finite-stratum clamp model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1]):P\text{ satisfies the conditional-density, stratum-mass, polynomial-thinning, and Hölder member conditions}\}\).

definitions.name: Information-balance bandwidth
definitions.construction: \(h_n=\inf\{h\in(0,1-\bar\delta]:n h^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h)^\kappa\geq1\}\), with \(h_n=1-\bar\delta\) if the set is empty.

definitions.name: Total-Gram-stabilized local-polynomial estimator
definitions.construction: Split the sample into \(I_0,I_1,I_2\). Set \(\widehat\nu_n=|I_0|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_0}Y_i\mathbf 1\{A_i>\delta_n\}\), \(\widehat b_x=|I_1|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i\leq\delta_n\}\), and \(\widetilde\mu_x=\Pi_{[0,1]}(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}Y_i)\) on \(\Omega_x\), with \(\widetilde\mu_x=1/2\) off \(\Omega_x\). Define \(\widehat\theta_n=\Pi_{[0,1]}[\widehat\nu_n+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_x\widetilde\mu_x]\).

definitions.name: Bias-aware atom-fallback interval
definitions.construction: Let \(t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}\), \(b_0=t_\alpha/\sqrt{|I_0|}\), and \(b_1=t_\alpha/\sqrt{|I_1|}\). For each \(x\), set \(B_x=Lh_n^\beta\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|+t_\alpha(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2)^{1/2}\) and \(D_x=(\widehat b_x+b_1)B_x+b_1\) on \(\Omega_x\), while \(D_x=\widehat b_x+b_1\) off \(\Omega_x\). Define \(\mathrm{CI}_n=[\widehat\theta_n-b_0-\sum_xD_x,\widehat\theta_n+b_0+\sum_xD_x]\cap[0,1]\).

definitions.name: Realized-design exact-modulus handle
definitions.construction: Condition on \(\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\), optimize affine intercept weights against the realized total Gram and the Hölder bias functional, calibrate the conditional bounded-outcome test, and integrate its excess length over the polynomial-thinning design law.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), the conditional pushforward law satisfies \(P\{d_\delta(A)\in\mathrm da\mid X=x\}=\pi_x(a)\mathbf 1\{a>\delta\}\,\mathrm da+q_x(\delta)\,\delta_\delta(\mathrm da)\), with \(c_-\delta^{\kappa+1}/(\kappa+1)\leq q_x(\delta)\leq c_+\delta^{\kappa+1}/(\kappa+1)\).
statements.justification: This cited setup specializes the threshold-LMTP pushforward calculation to the deterministic clamp and fixes the mixed dominating measure used to interpret the observed functional.
statements.gap: Díaz et al. supply threshold-LMTP identification, and McCoy et al. formulate clipped MTP ratios with an appropriate mixed dominating measure; this proposition claims no novelty beyond recording their specialization in the notation of the statistical frontier.
statements.consumer: The formula connects the observed-data target to the user-specified lower-threshold policy in the \(\texttt{lmtp}\) workflow.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\).  For every Borel set \(B\subseteq[0,1]\), Definition \texttt{def:clamp-policy} gives the disjoint inverse-image decomposition
\[
 \{d_\delta(A)\in B\}
 =\{A\in B\cap(\delta,1]\}
   \mathbin{\dot\cup}
   \bigl(\{A\in[0,\delta]\}\cap\{\delta\in B\}\bigr).
\]
By Assumption \texttt{ass:conditional-density-law}, conditional on \(X=x\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P\{d_\delta(A)\in B\mid X=x\}
 &=\int_{B\cap(\delta,1]}\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da
   +\mathbf 1\{\delta\in B\}\int_0^\delta\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\\
 &=\int_B\pi_x(a)\mathbf 1\{a>\delta\}\,\mathrm da
   +q_x(\delta)\delta_\delta(B),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the last equality is the definition of \(q_x\).  Equality on every Borel set proves the asserted equality of measures.  Finally, Assumption \texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning} and integration of its almost-everywhere inequalities give
\[
 \frac{c_-}{\kappa+1}\delta^{\kappa+1}
 =\int_0^\delta c_-a^\kappa\,\mathrm da
 \le q_x(\delta)
 \le\int_0^\delta c_+a^\kappa\,\mathrm da
 =\frac{c_+}{\kappa+1}\delta^{\kappa+1}.
\]
This also covers \(\delta=0\), when all three quantities vanish.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), \(d_\delta(A)\) lies in the support of the conditional natural-treatment law given \(X=x\) almost surely. At \(\delta=0\) this follows from the identity map; at \(\delta>0\) every neighborhood of \(\delta\) has positive conditional probability by conditional absolute continuity and the lower polynomial envelope.
statements.justification: The support statement records why no separate pointwise density-positivity assumption is needed for causal interpretation of the clamp.
statements.gap: This is the standard modified-policy support requirement specialized to a boundary-thinned continuous treatment law, not a novel statistical claim.
statements.consumer: The proposition discharges the positivity premise in the causal bridge while keeping causal assumptions outside the minimax model.
statements.proof_tex:
For a probability measure on \([0,1]\), call \(a\) a support point when every relatively open neighborhood of \(a\) has positive probability.  Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\).  If \(V\) is any relatively open neighborhood of any \(a\in[0,1]\), then \(V\) contains a nondegenerate interval \(I\subseteq[0,1]\).  Assumptions \texttt{ass:conditional-density-law} and \texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning} imply
\[
 P(A\in V\mid X=x)
 \geq \int_I\pi_x(t)\,\mathrm dt
 \geq c_-\int_I t^\kappa\,\mathrm dt>0.
\]
The last strict inequality holds also when the closure of \(I\) meets zero, because \(t^\kappa>0\) for every \(t>0\).  Thus the conditional natural-treatment support is all of \([0,1]\).  Definition \texttt{def:clamp-policy} gives \(d_\delta(A)\in[0,1]\) almost surely, so \(d_\delta(A)\) belongs to that support almost surely.  In particular, at \(\delta=0\) the map is the identity; when \(\delta>0\), the preceding display applied to every neighborhood of \(\delta\) verifies the claimed boundary support directly.

statements.statement: Let \(P^{\mathrm F}\) be a full-data causal law with observed margin \(P\in\mathcal M\). If the jointly measurable consistency, conditional exchangeability, extra author-imposed all-treatment causal-mean version, and modified-policy support premises hold, then for every \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), \(Y\{d_\delta(A)\}=Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}+Y(\delta)\mathbf 1\{A\leq\delta\}\) almost surely and \(\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}]+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_x^P(\delta)=\theta_\delta(P)\).
statements.justification: This setup proposition gives an optional full-data interpretation of the observed-data functional, conditional on an explicit author-imposed pointwise mean/version bridge that is not used by any statistical headline theorem.
statements.gap: Díaz et al. provide the LMTP identification template and standard causal premises, but not pointwise equality at every dose between causal means and a selected continuous observed-regression version; that non-testable compatibility restriction is imposed here only for interpretation and is not an incremental novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Applied users may interpret confidence intervals for \(\theta_\delta(P)\) as intervals for the clamp-policy mean only when joint-measurable consistency, exchangeability, policy support, and the extra author-imposed all-treatment mean/version equality are scientifically credible.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\).  Definition \texttt{def:clamp-policy} says that \(d_\delta(A)=A\) on \(\{A>\delta\}\) and \(d_\delta(A)=\delta\) on \(\{A\leq\delta\}\).  Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} therefore yields, almost surely,
\[
 Y\{d_\delta(A)\}
 =Y(A)\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}+Y(\delta)\mathbf 1\{A\leq\delta\}
 =Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}+Y(\delta)\mathbf 1\{A\leq\delta\}.
\]
All variables here are bounded and jointly measurable by Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency}, so the following conditional expectations exist.  Assumption \texttt{ass:exchangeability}, applied at the fixed treatment \(\delta\), gives for every stratum \(x\)
\[
 \mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(\delta)\mathbf 1\{A\leq\delta\}\mid X=x]
 =\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(\delta)\mid X=x]
   P(A\leq\delta\mid X=x).
\]
The first factor is \(\mu_x^P(\delta)\) by Assumption \texttt{ass:causal-mean-version}; the second is \(q_x(\delta)\) by Proposition \texttt{prop:pushforward-setup}.  Taking expectations in the preceding almost-sure identity, using that the observed margin of \(P^{\mathrm F}\) is \(P\), and summing over the finite stratum space gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})
 &=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}]
   +\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_x^P(\delta)\\
 &=\theta_\delta(P),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the last equality is the definition of \(\theta_\delta\).  Proposition \texttt{prop:policy-support} verifies that every realized modified treatment is in the conditional natural-treatment support; the displayed calculation additionally uses the explicitly imposed all-treatment mean version, so it does not infer a point value from an almost-everywhere regression version.

statements.statement: Uniformly over deterministic \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\), the bandwidth satisfies \(n h_n^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa\asymp1\) and the effective local count satisfies \(n h_n(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa\asymp h_n^{-2\beta}\). If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}\to\infty\), then \(h_n\asymp(n\delta_n^\kappa)^{-1/(2\beta+1)}\); if \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}=O(1)\), then \(h_n\asymp n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}\).
statements.justification: This balance converts polynomial thinning into the information scale that drives both estimation and inference.
statements.gap: Gaiffas derives the balance at a fixed degenerate point; the clamp requires a moving point \(\delta_n\) and an atom multiplier that changes the relevant phase boundary.
statements.consumer: The local-count identity is the normalization needed by the total-Gram probability bound and by bandwidth selection in the threshold-policy estimator.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(H=1-\bar\delta>0\) and
\[
 F_{n,\delta}(h)=n h^{2\beta+1}(\delta+h)^\kappa,
 \qquad 0<h\leq H.
\]
The restrictions \(\beta>0\) and \(\kappa\geq0\) make this function continuous and strictly increasing.  Moreover,
\[
 F_{n,\delta}(H)\geq nH^{2\beta+\kappa+1},
\]
uniformly in \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\).  Hence, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the set in Definition \texttt{def:bandwidth} is nonempty and its infimum is the unique solution of
\[
 n h_n^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa=1. \tag{1}
\]
This proves the first asserted comparison, in fact with equality for all such \(n\).  Dividing (1) by \(h_n^{2\beta}\) gives
\[
 n h_n(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa=h_n^{-2\beta}, \tag{2}
\]
which proves the effective-count assertion.

Let \(e_n=\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}=n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}\).  If \(\delta_n/e_n\to\infty\), set \(z_n=h_n/\delta_n\).  Equation (1) becomes
\[
 n\delta_n^{2\beta+\kappa+1}z_n^{2\beta+1}(1+z_n)^\kappa=1.
\]
Its first factor tends to infinity, so monotonicity forces \(z_n\to0\).  Substitution back into (1) yields
\[
 h_n^{2\beta+1}\sim(n\delta_n^\kappa)^{-1},
 \qquad
 h_n\asymp(n\delta_n^\kappa)^{-1/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
If instead \(d_n=\delta_n/e_n=O(1)\) and \(s_n=h_n/e_n\), then (1) is
\[
 s_n^{2\beta+1}(d_n+s_n)^\kappa=1. \tag{3}
\]
Because \(d_n\) is bounded, (3) bounds \(s_n\) above and away from zero by constants depending only on that bound and the declared exponents.  Thus \(h_n\asymp e_n=n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}\), as claimed.  Every comparison was uniform in the deterministic threshold within its stated regime.

statements.statement: The constant \(\lambda_\star\) is strictly positive. There are constants \(C,c>0\), depending only on the declared model constants, such that uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and deterministic \(\delta_n\), \(P(\Omega_x^c)\leq C\exp\{-c n h_n(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa\}\). On \(\Omega_x\), the exact intercept weights reproduce polynomials through degree \(\ell\) and obey \(\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|\leq C\) and \(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2\leq C/N_x\). No continuity or differentiability of \(\pi_x\) beyond two-sided polynomial comparability is required.
statements.justification: This is the early-kill lemma: it makes the singular-Gram fallback negligible at the atom-weighted target scale under measurable density envelopes alone.
statements.gap: Gaiffas stabilizes local polynomial Gram matrices under an exact regularly varying design; the present claim is uniform over every measurable density between two polynomial envelopes and controls the exact \(\ell_1\)- and \(\ell_2\)-weight norms.
statements.consumer: The lemma is the sole random-design input needed for the finite-sample honest interval and prevents an undocumented propensity-smoothness condition from entering the official workflow.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(d=\ell+1\), \(m=|I_2|\), \(\delta=\delta_n\), and \(h=h_n\).  First consider the reference matrices.  For every nonzero \(z\in\mathbb R^d\), the polynomial \(u\mapsto z^\top v_\ell(u)\) is nonzero except on a finite set.  Consequently,
\[
 z^\top M_{\kappa,\rho}z
 =\frac{\int_0^1\{z^\top v_\ell(u)\}^2(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}
        {\int_0^1(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}>0
\]
for every \(\rho\geq0\).  The entries are continuous in \(\rho\), and after dividing numerator and denominator by \(\rho^\kappa\) they converge as \(\rho\to\infty\) to the entries of \(\int_0^1v_\ell(u)v_\ell(u)^\top\,\mathrm du\), another positive-definite matrix.  Continuity of the smallest eigenvalue on the compactification \([0,\infty]\) therefore gives
\[
 \inf_{\rho\geq0}\lambda_{\min}(M_{\kappa,\rho})>0.
\]
Since \(c_->0\) and \(c_+<\infty\), the definition of \(\lambda_\star\) proves \(\lambda_\star>0\).

Let
\[
 s_x=P\{X=x,\delta\leq A\leq\delta+h\},
 \qquad \mu_{N,x}=ms_x.
\]
Assumptions \texttt{ass:stratum-mass}, \texttt{ass:conditional-density-law}, and \texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning} imply
\[
 c_1h(\delta+h)^\kappa\leq s_x\leq c_2h(\delta+h)^\kappa, \tag{4}
\]
where for the lower bound one integrates over \([\delta+h/2,\delta+h]\) and uses \(a^\kappa\geq2^{-\kappa}(\delta+h)^\kappa\).  Since \(m\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), (4) and Lemma \texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases} give
\[
 \mu_{N,x}\asymp nh(\delta+h)^\kappa\asymp h^{-2\beta}. \tag{5}
\]

By Assumption \texttt{ass:iid-sampling}, \(N_x\) is binomial with parameters \(m,s_x\).  Conditional on \(N_x=k>0\), the \(k\) local values \(U=(A-\delta)/h\) are independent with density proportional to \(u\mapsto\pi_x(\delta+hu)\) on \([0,1]\).  Let \(Q_x\) be the conditional second-moment matrix of \(v_\ell(U)\).  For every \(z\in\mathbb R^d\), Assumption \texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning} yields, with \(\rho=\delta/h\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 z^\top Q_xz
 &\geq\frac{c_-\int_0^1\{z^\top v_\ell(u)\}^2(\delta+hu)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}
              {c_+\int_0^1(\delta+hu)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}\\
 &=\frac{c_-}{c_+}z^\top M_{\kappa,\rho}z
 \geq\lambda_\star\lVert z\rVert_2^2.
 \end{aligned} \tag{6}
\]
This comparison uses only the two measurable density envelopes.

Each entry of \(v_\ell(U)v_\ell(U)^\top\) lies in \([0,1]\).  Applying the scalar exponential-Markov bound to each centered bounded entry and taking a union bound over the fixed \(d^2\) entries gives
\[
 P\left(\left.\left\|k^{-1}G_x-Q_x\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}>\lambda_\star/2\,\right|N_x=k\right)
 \leq 2d^2\exp(-c_0k), \tag{7}
\]
because the operator norm is at most \(d\) times the largest absolute entry.  On the complement of the event in (7), (6) implies \(\lambda_{\min}(G_x)\geq k\lambda_\star/2\).  The binomial generating function now gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(\Omega_x^c)
 &\leq C_0\mathbb E[\exp(-c_0N_x)]\\
 &=C_0\{1-s_x+s_xe^{-c_0}\}^{m}
 \leq C_0\exp\{-c_1ms_x\}\\
 &\leq C\exp\{-cnh(\delta+h)^\kappa\},
 \end{aligned} \tag{8}
\]
where (4) was used in the last line.  This includes the event \(N_x=0\).

It remains to verify the exact weight statements.  On \(\Omega_x\), for \(0\leq j\leq\ell\),
\[
 \sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}U_i^j
 =e_0^\top G_x^{-1}\left\{\sum_{i:X_i=x,\,0\leq U_i\leq1}v_\ell(U_i)U_i^j\right\}
 =e_0^\top G_x^{-1}G_xe_j
 =\mathbf 1\{j=0\}. \tag{9}
\]
Furthermore, \(\lVert v_\ell(u)\rVert_2\leq\sqrt d\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\lVert G_x^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2/(\lambda_\star N_x)\), whence
\[
 \sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|
 \leq N_x\frac{2\sqrt d}{\lambda_\star N_x}
 \leq C, \tag{10}
\]
and, using the definition of \(G_x\),
\[
 \sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2
 =e_0^\top G_x^{-1}G_xG_x^{-1}e_0
 =e_0^\top G_x^{-1}e_0
 \leq\frac{2}{\lambda_\star N_x}. \tag{11}
\]
Equations (8)--(11) prove every assertion with constants depending only on the declared model constants.

statements.statement: There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the declared model constants, such that for every deterministic threshold sequence and all sufficiently large \(n\), \(c r_n\leq R_n^\star\leq\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_n-\theta_{\delta_n}(P)|\leq C r_n\). The lower bound is the maximum, and therefore the same order as the sum, of a same-class global Bernoulli shift yielding \(n^{-1/2}\) separation and a same-class localized Bernoulli regression perturbation of width \(h_n\) yielding \(\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta\) separation with bounded product divergence.
statements.justification: The theorem gives the exact order frontier for the unsmoothed clamp target, including both its regular and point-evaluation components.
statements.gap: Gaiffas establishes an unweighted fixed-point regression rate under a degenerate random design, while Díaz et al. identify the threshold-LMTP mean without a minimax rate; McCoy et al. analyze a stochastic-shift effect-modifier target under high-probability regularity. None gives the matched risk frontier for the observed retained-natural-course mean plus an atom-weighted moving point evaluation.
statements.consumer: An analyst using the lower-threshold \(\texttt{lmtp}\) policy obtains the first threshold-sequence-specific accuracy benchmark without replacing the policy by a stochastic region average.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(\delta=\delta_n\), \(h=h_n\), and \(b_x=p_xq_x(\delta)\).  Proposition \texttt{prop:pushforward-setup} gives
\[
 0\leq b_x\leq C\delta^{\kappa+1}. \tag{12}
\]
We first prove the upper bound for the explicit estimator in Definition \texttt{def:total-gram-estimator}.  Since all three blocks have order \(n\), Assumption \texttt{ass:iid-sampling} and the variance bound for a \([0,1]\)-valued variable give
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\nu_n-\nu_\delta(P)|\leq Cn^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat b_x-b_x|\leq Cn^{-1/2}. \tag{13}
\]

On \(\Omega_x\), let \(S_x=\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}Y_i\).  By the polynomial reproduction identity in Lemma \texttt{lem:total-gram}, the Taylor polynomial of \(\mu_x^P\) at \(\delta\) contributes exactly \(\mu_x^P(\delta)\).  Assumption \texttt{ass:holder-regression} and the weight bounds in that lemma therefore imply, conditionally on the realized \((X_i,A_i)\)'s,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|\mathbb E_P[S_x\mid (X_i,A_i)_{i\in I_2}]-\mu_x^P(\delta)\right|
 &\leq Lh^\beta\sum_i|w_{ix}|\leq Ch^\beta,\\
 \operatorname{Var}_P(S_x\mid (X_i,A_i)_{i\in I_2})
 &\leq\frac14\sum_iw_{ix}^2\leq\frac{C}{N_x}. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{14}
\]
Projection onto \([0,1]\) cannot increase distance from \(\mu_x^P(\delta)\in[0,1]\).  If \(\mu_{N,x}=\mathbb E_PN_x\), a scalar exponential-Markov calculation for the binomial count gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left[N_x^{-1/2}\mathbf 1\{N_x>0\}\right]
 \leq (2/\mu_{N,x})^{1/2}+P(N_x<\mu_{N,x}/2)
 \leq C\mu_{N,x}^{-1/2}. \tag{15}
\]
Equations (2), (4), and (5) from the preceding lemmas give \(\mu_{N,x}^{-1/2}\leq Ch^\beta\).  On \(\Omega_x^c\), both the fallback and the true regression value lie in \([0,1]\); Lemma \texttt{lem:total-gram} and the elementary bound \(e^{-ct}\leq C_ct^{-1/2}\), with \(t=h^{-2\beta}\), show that its expected contribution is at most \(Ch^\beta\).  Thus (14)--(15) yield
\[
 \mathbb E_P|\widetilde\mu_x-\mu_x^P(\delta)|\leq Ch^\beta. \tag{16}
\]

The three blocks are independent.  Before the final projection, add and subtract \(b_x\widetilde\mu_x\), use \(0\leq\widetilde\mu_x\leq1\), and apply (12)--(16):
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_n-\theta_\delta(P)|
 &\leq \mathbb E_P|\widehat\nu_n-\nu_\delta(P)|
 +\sum_x\left\{\mathbb E_P|\widehat b_x-b_x|
 +b_x\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\mu_x-\mu_x^P(\delta)|\right\}\\
 &\leq C\{n^{-1/2}+\delta^{\kappa+1}h^\beta\}=Cr_n.
\end{aligned} \tag{17}
\]
The first inequality remains valid after projection because \(\theta_\delta(P)\in[0,1]\).  Taking the supremum proves the minimax upper bound with one data-driven estimator.

For the converse, we give two explicit same-class experiments.  In both, take \(p_x=1/J\) and \(\pi_x(a)=(\kappa+1)a^\kappa\) for every \(x\).  These choices obey Assumptions \texttt{ass:stratum-mass} and \texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning} because \(p_{\min}\leq1/J\) and \(c_-\leq\kappa+1\leq c_+\).  First let the conditional outcome be Bernoulli with constant mean \(1/2\) under \(P_0\) and \(1/2+a_0n^{-1/2}\) under \(P_1\), for a fixed sufficiently small \(a_0>0\).  Both regressions satisfy Assumption \texttt{ass:holder-regression}, and the definition of \(\theta_\delta\) gives
\[
 |\theta_\delta(P_1)-\theta_\delta(P_0)|=a_0n^{-1/2}. \tag{18}
\]
The one-observation chi-square divergence is \(4a_0^2/n\), hence
\[
 \chi^2(P_1^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 =(1+4a_0^2/n)^n-1\leq e^{4a_0^2}-1. \tag{19}
\]

For the localized experiment, choose a nonnegative \(C^\infty\) function \(\varphi\), supported on \([-1,1]\), with \(\varphi(0)=1\).  The scaled functions \(h^\beta\varphi((\,cdot-\delta)/h)\), restricted to \([0,1]\), have Taylor-remainder Hölder norm at most a finite constant \(C_{\varphi,\beta}\): this follows directly by scaling the Taylor remainder when \(\beta\) is an integer and by scaling the Hölder modulus of the highest derivative otherwise.  Set
\[
 \mu_0(a)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_1(a)=\frac12+a_1h^\beta\varphi((a-\delta)/h), \tag{20}
\]
for every stratum, where \(a_1>0\) is small enough that \(a_1C_{\varphi,\beta}\leq L\) and \(a_1h^\beta\lVert\varphi\rVert_\infty\leq1/4\).  Taking Bernoulli outcomes with these means produces two members of the same \(\mathcal M\).  Their one-observation chi-square divergence satisfies
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \chi^2(P_1,P_0)
 &=4\int_0^1\{\mu_1(a)-\mu_0(a)\}^2(\kappa+1)a^\kappa\,\mathrm da\\
 &\leq Ca_1^2h^{2\beta+1}(\delta+h)^\kappa.
 \end{aligned} \tag{21}
\]
Definition \texttt{def:bandwidth} and Lemma \texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases} make \(n\) times the last expression at most \(Ca_1^2\).  Thus
\[
 \chi^2(P_1^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq \exp(Ca_1^2)-1. \tag{22}
\]
Since the perturbation is nonnegative and \(q_x(\delta)=\delta^{\kappa+1}\) for this design, the observed functional has separation
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \theta_\delta(P_1)-\theta_\delta(P_0)
 &=\int_\delta^1\{\mu_1(a)-\mu_0(a)\}(\kappa+1)a^\kappa\,\mathrm da
   +\delta^{\kappa+1}\{\mu_1(\delta)-\mu_0(\delta)\}\\
 &\geq a_1\delta^{\kappa+1}h^\beta. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{23}
\]

For completeness, if \(Q_1\ll Q_0\) with likelihood ratio \(Z\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives for every event \(E\)
\[
 |Q_1(E)-Q_0(E)|=|\mathbb E_{Q_0}[(Z-1)\mathbf 1_E]|
 \leq\{\mathbb E_{Q_0}(Z-1)^2\}^{1/2}=\sqrt{\chi^2(Q_1,Q_0)}. \tag{24}
\]
Choose \(a_0,a_1\) so that the right sides of (19) and (22) have square roots at most \(1/2\).  For any estimator \(T\) and either pair, let \(\Delta\) denote its target separation and let \(E=\{|T-\theta(P_0)|<\Delta/2\}\).  Then
\[
 \max_{j=0,1}\mathbb E_{P_j}|T-\theta(P_j)|
 \geq\frac{\Delta}{4}\{P_0^{\otimes n}(E^c)+P_1^{\otimes n}(E)\}
 \geq\frac{\Delta}{4}(1-1/2). \tag{25}
\]
Equations (18) and (23), applied separately and then maximized, show
\[
 R_n^\star\geq c\max\{n^{-1/2},\delta^{\kappa+1}h^\beta\}
 \geq \frac c2\{n^{-1/2}+\delta^{\kappa+1}h^\beta\}=c'r_n. \tag{26}
\]
Together, (17) and (26) prove the theorem and explicitly exhibit the announced global-shift and localized-Bernoulli mechanisms.

statements.statement: For every \(n\) large enough, \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_n\}\geq1-\alpha\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)]\leq C r_n\). Conversely, every confidence interval with coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M\) satisfies \(L_n^\star\geq c r_n\). The interval adapts the bias-aware construction of Armstrong and Kolesár to the distinct polynomially thinned random-design clamp functional and remains honest on singular-Gram realizations through the atom fallback.
statements.justification: Risk optimality alone does not justify uncertainty quantification for a nonregular target; the confidence-length statement makes honesty a theorem-level deliverable.
statements.gap: Armstrong and Kolesár calibrate smoothing bias for nonparametric regression under fixed-design formulations, Gaiffas does not construct honest intervals, and McCoy et al.'s high-probability regularity theory does not give uniformly honest expected length. None integrates a random singular-Gram event at a shrinking atom-mass scale.
statements.consumer: The interval replaces the invalid Wald output that a continuous threshold policy can otherwise produce in the \(\texttt{lmtp}\) workflow.
statements.proof_tex:
Again write \(\delta=\delta_n\), \(h=h_n\), and \(b_x=p_xq_x(\delta)\).  Consider the following simultaneous events:
\[
 \begin{split}
 E_0&=\{|\widehat\nu_n-\nu_\delta(P)|\leq b_0\},\\
 E_{1x}&=\{|\widehat b_x-b_x|\leq b_1\},\\
 E_{2x}&=\Omega_x^c\ \cup\ 
 \left\{\left|\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}Y_i-\mu_x^P(\delta)\right|\leq B_x\right\}.
 \end{split} \tag{27}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:iid-sampling}, boundedness, and the exponential-Markov argument for a bounded sample mean give
\[
 P(E_0^c)\leq2e^{-2|I_0|b_0^2}=\frac{\alpha}{6J},
 \qquad
 P(E_{1x}^c)\leq2e^{-2|I_1|b_1^2}=\frac{\alpha}{6J}. \tag{28}
\]
On \(\Omega_x\), condition on the realized treatment design in \(I_2\).  The outcome residuals are independent, have conditional mean zero for almost every realized design point by the defining version property of \(\mu_x^P\), and each weighted residual has range length \(|w_{ix}|\).  Hence
\[
 P\left(\left.\left|\sum_iw_{ix}\{Y_i-\mu_x^P(A_i)\}\right|>
 t_\alpha\Bigl(\sum_iw_{ix}^2\Bigr)^{1/2}\,\right|(X_i,A_i)_{i\in I_2}\right)
 \leq2e^{-2t_\alpha^2}=\frac{\alpha}{6J}. \tag{29}
\]
Polynomial reproduction from Lemma \texttt{lem:total-gram} and Assumption \texttt{ass:holder-regression} bound the conditional bias by \(Lh^\beta\sum_i|w_{ix}|\).  Thus (29) proves \(P(E_{2x}^c)\leq\alpha/(6J)\).  A union bound gives
\[
 P\left(E_0\cap\bigcap_x(E_{1x}\cap E_{2x})\right)
 \geq1-\frac{(2J+1)\alpha}{6J}\geq1-\alpha. \tag{30}
\]

On the event in (30), projection onto \([0,1]\) cannot enlarge the local regression error.  If \(\Omega_x\) occurs, then
\[
 |\widehat b_x\widetilde\mu_x-b_x\mu_x^P(\delta)|
 \leq b_1+(\widehat b_x+b_1)B_x=D_x. \tag{31}
\]
If \(\Omega_x^c\) occurs, the two products belong respectively to \([0,\widehat b_x]\) and \([0,b_x]\); therefore
\[
 |\widehat b_x\widetilde\mu_x-b_x\mu_x^P(\delta)|
 \leq\max\{\widehat b_x,b_x\}
 \leq\widehat b_x+b_1=D_x. \tag{32}
\]
Combining (31)--(32) with \(E_0\), and using contraction of the final projection about \(\theta_\delta(P)\in[0,1]\), yields
\[
 |\widehat\theta_n-\theta_\delta(P)|\leq b_0+\sum_xD_x. \tag{33}
\]
Definitions \texttt{def:total-gram-estimator} and \texttt{def:honest-interval} now show that (33) is exactly the event \(\theta_\delta(P)\in\mathrm{CI}_n\).  Equation (30) proves uniform finite-sample honesty for every sufficiently large \(n\).

We next bound expected length, including the singular-Gram realizations.  The inverse-binomial estimate (15) and Lemma \texttt{lem:total-gram} imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_x\mathbf 1\{\Omega_x\}]
 \leq CLh^\beta+Ct_\alpha\mathbb E_P[N_x^{-1/2}\mathbf 1\{N_x>0\}]
 \leq Ch^\beta. \tag{34}
\]
The split makes \(\widehat b_x\) independent of \(B_x\) and \(\Omega_x\), while \(\mathbb E_P\widehat b_x=b_x\).  Therefore the two branches in Definition \texttt{def:honest-interval} give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_PD_x
 &\leq(b_x+b_1)\mathbb E_P[B_x\mathbf 1\{\Omega_x\}]+b_1
 +(b_x+b_1)P(\Omega_x^c)\\
 &\leq C\{n^{-1/2}+b_xh^\beta\}\\
 &\leq C\{n^{-1/2}+\delta^{\kappa+1}h^\beta\}. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{35}
\]
Here Proposition \texttt{prop:pushforward-setup} bounds \(b_x\), Lemma \texttt{lem:total-gram} bounds the bad-event probability by \(Ce^{-ch^{-2\beta}}\), and \(e^{-ch^{-2\beta}}\leq Ch^\beta\).  Intersecting with \([0,1]\) cannot increase length, so (35), the fixed value of \(J\), and \(b_0=O(n^{-1/2})\) yield
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)]
 \leq2b_0+2\sum_x\mathbb E_PD_x
 \leq Cr_n. \tag{36}
\]

It remains to prove the converse for every uniformly honest interval \(C_n\).  Reuse the two explicit same-class pairs constructed in the proof of Theorem \texttt{thm:minimax-risk}, decreasing their fixed perturbation amplitudes if necessary so that, by (19), (22), and (24), their product-law total variation is at most some \(\eta<(1-2\alpha)/2\).  Let their two target values be \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), with separation \(\Delta\).  Uniform coverage implies
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_0^{\otimes n}\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in C_n\}
 &\geq P_0^{\otimes n}\{\theta_0\in C_n\}
   +P_0^{\otimes n}\{\theta_1\in C_n\}-1\\
 &\geq(1-\alpha)+(1-\alpha-\eta)-1
 =1-2\alpha-\eta>0. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{37}
\]
On this event an interval has length at least \(\Delta\), and hence
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{len}(C_n)]
 \geq \Delta(1-2\alpha-\eta). \tag{38}
\]
For the global pair, \(\Delta\asymp n^{-1/2}\); for the localized pair, \(\Delta\geq c\delta^{\kappa+1}h^\beta\).  Taking the maximum of the two lower bounds and using \(\max(u,v)\geq(u+v)/2\) proves \(L_n^\star\geq cr_n\).  Together with (30) and (36), this proves all three claims, including the atom-weighted control of singular-Gram realizations.

statements.statement: The phase boundary satisfies \(\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}/\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}\to\infty\). If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to0\), then \(r_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\) (regular regime). If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to c\in(0,\infty)\), both summands of \(r_n\) have order \(n^{-1/2}\) (critical regime). If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to\infty\) and \(\delta_n\to0\), then \(r_n\asymp\delta_n^{\kappa+1}(n\delta_n^\kappa)^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\) (atom-dominated regime). If \(\delta_n\to\delta_0\in(0,\bar\delta]\), then \(r_n\asymp n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\) (fixed-threshold regime). At \(\delta_n=0\), \(q_x(0)=0\), \(\theta_0(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y]\), and the construction reduces to bounded-mean inference at rate \(n^{-1/2}\).
statements.justification: The phase diagram states when the published root-\(n\) paradigm is valid, critical, or false for the exact clamp.
statements.gap: Existing LMTP theory separates pathwise differentiable policies from excluded threshold policies but supplies no quantitative boundary between regular and atom-dominated sequences.
statements.consumer: The four regimes tell an applied user whether a threshold choice supports ordinary precision, requires the bias-aware atom interval, or behaves like a fixed nonparametric point target.
statements.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 D=\beta\kappa+2\beta+\kappa+1,
 \qquad
 e_n=\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n},
 \qquad
 c_n=\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}.
\]
The definitions give
\[
 \frac{c_n}{e_n}
 =n^{1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)-1/(2D)}\longrightarrow\infty, \tag{39}
\]
because \(2D-(2\beta+\kappa+1)=2\beta\kappa+2\beta+\kappa+1>0\).

When \(\delta_n\gtrsim e_n\), Lemma \texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases} and its balance equation give, up to constants,
\[
 \delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
 \asymp n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}
 \delta_n^{D/(2\beta+1)}. \tag{40}
\]
At \(\delta_n=c_n\), the right side equals \(n^{-1/2}\), since \(c_n^D=n^{-1/2}\).  When \(\delta_n=O(e_n)\), the same lemma gives
\[
 \delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
 \leq C e_n^{\beta+\kappa+1}
 =o(n^{-1/2}), \tag{41}
\]
because \((\beta+\kappa+1)/(2\beta+\kappa+1)>1/2\).

Equations (39)--(41) settle all moving-threshold cases.  If \(\delta_n/c_n\to0\), the atom term is \(o(n^{-1/2})\), whether \(\delta_n=O(e_n)\) by (41) or \(\delta_n\gtrsim e_n\) by (40); thus \(r_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\).  If \(\delta_n/c_n\to c\in(0,\infty)\), then (39) places the sequence above the edge scale and (40) makes the atom term of order \(n^{-1/2}\).  If \(\delta_n/c_n\to\infty\) while \(\delta_n\to0\), then again \(\delta_n/e_n\to\infty\), and (40) dominates the root-\(n\) term, giving
\[
 r_n\asymp\delta_n^{\kappa+1}(n\delta_n^\kappa)^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
If \(\delta_n\to\delta_0\in(0,\bar\delta]\), Lemma \texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases} gives \(h_n\asymp n^{-1/(2\beta+1)}\); the atom term then dominates and \(r_n\asymp n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\).  Theorem \texttt{thm:minimax-risk} and Theorem \texttt{thm:honest-length} transfer each of these comparisons to both minimax risk and minimax honest expected length.

Finally, when \(\delta_n=0\), Proposition \texttt{prop:pushforward-setup} gives \(q_x(0)=0\).  Conditional absolute continuity gives \(P(A=0)=0\), so the definition of \(\theta_0\) yields
\[
 \theta_0(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>0\}]=\mathbb E_PY.
\]
In Definition \texttt{def:total-gram-estimator}, \(\widehat b_x=0\) almost surely and \(\widehat\nu_n\) is the bounded sample mean on \(I_0\); the remaining interval padding is of root-\(n\) order by (35).  Hence the construction is bounded-mean inference at rate \(n^{-1/2}\), exactly as asserted.

statements.statement: In the one-stratum model with \(\beta=\kappa=1\) and \(\pi(a)=2a\), whenever \(\delta_n\gg n^{-1/4}\), \(h_n\asymp(n\delta_n)^{-1/3}\), the localized Bernoulli alternatives have product Kullback--Leibler divergence of order \(n\delta_n h_n^3\), and their target separation is of order \(\delta_n^2h_n\). The regular-to-atom transition is exactly \(\delta_n\asymp n^{-1/10}\).
statements.justification: This explicit calibration is the requested early-kill test and checks the general exponents against a transparent design.
statements.gap: No cited LMTP or degenerate-design result computes this atom-attenuated transition for the deterministic clamp mean.
statements.consumer: The calibration supplies a simulation benchmark and a unit test for an implementation of the proposed interval.
statements.proof_tex:
In this model, \(\beta=\kappa=1\), so
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}=n^{-1/4},
 \qquad
 \delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}
 =n^{-1/[2(1+2+1+1)]}=n^{-1/10}. \tag{42}
\]
When \(\delta_n\gg n^{-1/4}\), Lemma \texttt{lem:bandwidth-phases} gives
\[
 h_n\asymp(n\delta_n)^{-1/3},
 \qquad h_n/\delta_n\to0. \tag{43}
\]
For the localized alternatives (20), the regression displacement has height of order \(h_n\) and support width of order \(h_n\).  If \(|g|\leq1/4\), two applications of the mean-value theorem to the Bernoulli log likelihood give
\[
 c g^2\leq
 \operatorname{KL}\{\operatorname{Ber}(1/2+g),\operatorname{Ber}(1/2)\}
 \leq Cg^2,
\]
because the second derivative is bounded above and away from zero on \([1/4,3/4]\).  Since \(\pi(a)=2a\) and (43) makes \(a\asymp\delta_n\) throughout the effective local window, the one-observation Bernoulli divergence is therefore of order
\[
 h_n^2\int_{\delta_n-h_n}^{\delta_n+h_n}2a\,\mathrm da
 \asymp\delta_nh_n^3.
\]
Independence therefore makes the product Kullback--Leibler divergence of order \(n\delta_nh_n^3\), which is constant by (43).  The clamp atom has mass
\[
 q(\delta_n)=\int_0^{\delta_n}2a\,\mathrm da=\delta_n^2.
\]
Its regression displacement is of order \(h_n\), so its target contribution is of order \(\delta_n^2h_n\); the retained-course contribution is only of order \(\delta_nh_n^2=o(\delta_n^2h_n)\) by (43).  Thus the total target separation is of order \(\delta_n^2h_n\), agreeing with Theorem \texttt{thm:minimax-risk}.  Equating this quantity with \(n^{-1/2}\), and using (43), gives
\[
 \delta_n^2(n\delta_n)^{-1/3}=n^{-1/2}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \delta_n^{5/3}=n^{-1/6}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \delta_n=n^{-1/10},
\]
which proves the stated transition and agrees with Theorem \texttt{thm:phase-diagram}.

statements.statement: Does the realized-design exact-modulus handle yield the sharp asymptotic minimax constant for \(L_n^\star/r_n\) uniformly over all limits of \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\), while retaining the measurable two-sided density envelope and bounded outcomes? Equivalently, can one replace the conservative split-sample Hoeffding calibration by a conditional modulus interval whose worst-case expected length matches a least-favorable mixed regular-plus-local experiment in the regular, critical, atom-dominated, and fixed-threshold regimes?
statements.justification: The order-optimal interval leaves a genuine decision-theoretic question: the exact confidence-length constant when regular and atom experiments coexist.
statements.gap: Armstrong and Kolesár solve a fixed-design convex modulus, while the present experiment has a random total Gram, a moving atom weight, and a regular empirical-mean component.
statements.consumer: A sharp constant would determine the shortest defensible interval and the optimal critical value for a production-quality threshold-policy implementation.

sampling_model.design: Independent random design with fixed finite \(X\)-strata and continuous \(A\).
sampling_model.treatment: The observed-data target is \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\) for the exact deterministic map \(d_{\delta_n}(a)=\max\{a,\delta_n\}\); it is neither smoothed nor replaced.
sampling_model.overlap: Within every stratum, \(P(A\in B\mid X=x)=\int_B\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\) for every Borel \(B\subseteq[0,1]\), and the explicit novel treatment-assignment class imposes the global measurable envelope \(c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa\), allowing polynomial boundary thinning and bounded measurable departures from an exact power density.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite-stratum empirical atom masses and a sample-split local polynomial of order \(\ell\); no propensity estimator or propensity smoothness condition is imposed.

tldr: The first novel result is the matched minimax-risk and uniformly honest expected-length frontier \(n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta\) for the observed-data target \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta_n\}]+\sum_x p_xq_x(\delta_n)\mu_x^P(\delta_n)\), where \(n h_n^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa\asymp1\). On a fixed finite-stratum Hölder model with the explicit novel treatment-assignment envelope \(c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa\), a total-Gram-stabilized local polynomial, an atom-specific singular-design fallback, and same-class global-shift and localized-Bernoulli lower bounds yield the regular, critical, atom-dominated, and fixed-threshold regimes. These statistical headline theorems are observed-data-only. The conditional pushforward is a cited specialization of Díaz et al.; consistent with McCoy et al., clipping mass is represented relative to an appropriate mixed dominating measure. Equality of \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\) to the exact deterministic clamp-policy mean consumed by the official \(\texttt{lmtp}\) workflow is only an optional full-data interpretation, conditional on standard causal premises and an extra author-imposed, pointwise, non-testable equality between potential-outcome means and the declared continuous observed-regression version. That equality is not implied by consistency, exchangeability, policy support, observed-regression Hölder smoothness, or Díaz et al., and is not a novelty contribution.

project_justification.gap: Published LMTP identification covers the deterministic clamp, but its continuous-exposure efficiency theory does not provide rates for that non-pathwise-differentiable target. McCoy et al. correctly accommodate clipping mass through an appropriate dominating measure and a classification estimator of the pushforward law, but their stochastic-shift effect-modifier target and high-probability regularity theory do not provide a deterministic moving-clamp minimax or uniformly honest expected-length frontier. Degenerate-design regression theory treats an unweighted fixed point, and bias-aware confidence-interval theory does not integrate this atom-weighted random-design problem.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied object is the observed functional \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\) induced by the exact unsmoothed clamp under polynomial generalized-propensity thinning, with a threshold that may follow any deterministic sequence and with inference honest across the transition where the shrinking atom becomes first-order.
project_justification.fill: The known mixed-measure representation fixes the observed functional \(\theta_\delta(P)\); the novel global measurable polynomial envelope defines a treatment-assignment class containing beta-type boundary-thinning designs and bounded measurable tilts; the information-balance bandwidth and total-Gram lemma give an estimator on that class; two same-class experiments certify the minimax risk and confidence-length order; and the phase diagram converts those bounds into policy-facing regimes.

related_work: Díaz, Williams, Hoffman, and Schenck identify threshold-LMTP means by sequential regression and show that the continuous threshold example is not pathwise differentiable. Their result supplies the identification template and standard causal premises, but it does not supply pointwise equality at every dose between causal means and a selected continuous observed-regression version. The pushforward formula is a cited specialization, while the optional full-data bridge is conditional on that extra author-imposed, pointwise, non-testable compatibility restriction; neither setup statement nor the restriction is a novelty contribution. The statistical target and headline frontier theorems are observed-data-only, and Díaz et al. do not derive a risk or confidence-length frontier for deterministic threshold sequences. Hoffman et al. repeat the piecewise-invertibility boundary in their applied tutorial, and Williams and Díaz document the \(\texttt{lmtp}\) user-policy workflow that consumes the proposed result. McCoy et al.'s MTP density ratio is a Radon--Nikodym derivative with respect to an appropriate dominating measure, expressly allowing clipping-induced boundary mass, and their classification estimator targets the clipped pushforward law directly. Their object is a stochastic-shift effect-modifier target, and their high-probability regularity theory does not deliver the minimax risk or uniformly honest expected-length frontier for the deterministic clamp with an arbitrary moving threshold. Gaiffas derives the fixed-point regression rate and stabilized local polynomials under regularly varying degenerate random design. The global measurable envelope \(c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa\) used here is an explicit novel treatment-assignment class, not a consequence attributed to regular variation; together with the exact conditional-density identity for every Borel set, it permits bounded measurable deviations from exact power behavior while retaining controlled boundary thinning. Armstrong and Kolesár construct bias-aware honest intervals for nonparametric regression under fixed-design formulations; the observed mixed functional \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\), vanishing random design, moving point, and singular-Gram expected-length integration are absent. Kennedy et al. motivate two-stage causal local regression, while Bonvini and Kennedy study dose-response rates under smooth positive conditional densities rather than polynomial thinning. Van der Laan, Zhang, and Gilbert obtain root-\(n\) bands for a support-restricted stochastic region-average threshold response, a different estimand not used as a comparator target. Shahu et al. extend simultaneous LMTP inference under piecewise invertibility rather than the continuous threshold map.
technical_internal_limitation: The expected-length theorem requires the Hölder radius and thinning exponent to be declared. Adaptation to unknown \(\beta\) and \(\kappa\) is a separate ordered-modulus problem and may require a logarithmic payment. The exact-constant question also remains open; the primary claims concern sharp order uniformly over deterministic threshold sequences.
honest_scope: The proposal fixes a finite number of strata, a bounded outcome, known smoothness radius, and known thinning exponent. Its statistical minimax and honest-length claims concern only the observed-data model and require no causal premise. The clamp-policy equality is an optional interpretation requiring a jointly measurable potential-outcome process, \(Y=Y(A)\), conditional exchangeability, policy support, and the extra author-imposed pointwise equality of the causal mean with \(\mu_x^P(a)\) for every treatment value. This equality is non-testable, is credible only when the scientific model posits a well-defined intervention and a smooth structural conditional-mean response at every dose, and is not implied by consistency, exchangeability, support, observed-regression Hölder smoothness, continuity alone, or Díaz et al. It is not a novelty contribution. The proposal proves no longitudinal recursion, no simultaneous band over a continuum of thresholds, and no claim about the validity or invalidity of McCoy et al.'s dominating-measure density-ratio estimator for their stochastic-shift effect-modifier target. The reduction \(\delta_n=0\) gives the ordinary bounded sample-mean problem, while any fixed positive threshold reduces the irregular component to the Gaiffas pointwise exponent multiplied by a nonvanishing atom mass.
